$comment: Pre-existing operator actions with no reachable audit write (lint:audit-log).
This list may only SHRINK. Adding an entry means accepting a mutating
operator action whose occurrence leaves no trace — fix it or write a
`// @no-audit-required: <reason>` comment above the export instead.
MEASURED 2026-08-16, first run: 88 "use server" modules scanned, 37
operator+mutating actions derived, 25 already reach an audit write. These
12 are DEBT, not a verdict — each still owes a decision, and the three
shapes they fall into are NOT equally defensible:
· case-operator (addCaseNote/closeCase) — the fact lands in the
append-only case_events spine, which carries its own actor. Arguably
covered by a different ledger; needs a PO call on whether the
accountability query is expected to find it in audit_log.
· admin-proposals, service-offerings, revocation-evidence — the mutated
row itself records who acted (approval_requests, offerings), so the
trail exists but is not queryable alongside every other operator act.
· alert-subscriptions, novedades, outbox retry — operator preferences,
a read watermark, and a delivery retry. The weakest case for an audit
row, and the best candidates for an explicit @no-audit-required.
Regenerate with: pnpm tsx scripts/check-audit-log-coverage.ts --write-baseline
(only ever to SHRINK the list — the fence fails on a stale entry, so a
fixed action must be removed here in the same commit that fixes it.)
